source.title: A letter to my mother (ladder unit, machine-drafted)
source.author: Go course authors (drafted by an AI model)
source.attribution: Course-authored controlled Church Latin. Drafted by an AI model; not yet reviewed by a Latinist.
source.provenance: Drafted by an AI model for the course ladder in simple Ecclesiastical (Church) Latin; not reviewed by a Latinist. It is controlled, deliberately repetitive Latin written for learners and may contain unidiomatic phrasing. The English lines are the drafter's own.
source.licenseNote: Owned by the course authors; machine-drafted, not yet reviewed by a Latinist.

review.notes: Machine-drafted by an AI model; awaiting review by a Latinist. House style: simple Church Latin, spelled without macrons, with u/v and i/j as in Stage 0 (v and i only); present tense, with a few perfects (venit, vidit, fuit, dixit) in the last units.

english.source: drafted with the text; not reviewed

sentences.text: Samuel in domo est. Samuel in mensa epistulam scribit. Mater longe est.
sentences.english: Samuel is in the house. Samuel writes a letter at the table. His mother is far away.

sentences.text: Mater cara, salve!
sentences.english: Dear mother, hello!

sentences.text: Ego bene valeo. In urbe nova sum. Urbs bona est.
sentences.english: I am well. I am in a new town. The town is good.

sentences.text: Domus mea parva est, sed bona est. In domo mensam habeo. Fenestram quoque habeo.
sentences.english: My house is small, but it is good. In the house I have a table. I have a window too.

sentences.text: Hic amicos habeo. Anna amica mea est, et in valetudinario laborat. Lucius magister est, et in schola laborat. Martha panem et lac vendit. Marcus puer bonus est.
sentences.english: Here I have friends. Anna is my friend. She works at the clinic. Lucius is a teacher, and he works at school. Martha sells bread and milk. Marcus is a good boy.

sentences.text: Quomodo vales, mater cara? Et pater, quomodo valet? Ubi est frater meus? Ubi est soror mea?
sentences.english: How are you, dear mother? And father, how is he? Where is my brother? Where is my sister?

sentences.text: Cras ad ecclesiam eo, et gratias Deo ago. Hodie panem et lac habeo. Bene est.
sentences.english: Tomorrow I go to church, and I give thanks to God. Today I have bread and milk. It is well.

sentences.text: Scribe mihi, mater!
sentences.english: Write to me, mother!

sentences.text: Vale! Pax tibi, mater. Pax tibi, pater.
sentences.english: Goodbye! Peace to you, mother. Peace to you, father.

sentences.text: Samuel tuus
sentences.english: Your Samuel

sentences.text: Samuel in foro est. Martha Samuelem videt.
sentences.english: Samuel is in the market. Martha sees Samuel.

sentences.text: Salve, Samuel! Quid est hoc? Estne epistula?
sentences.english: Hello, Samuel! What is this? Is it a letter?
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Epistula est. Matri meae scribo. Hodie scribo.
sentences.english: It is a letter. I am writing to my mother. Today I write.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Bene! Urbs nova bona est, et hic amicos habes.
sentences.english: Good! The new town is good, and here you have friends.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Amicos bonos habeo, et gratias Deo ago.
sentences.english: I have good friends, and I give thanks to God.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Scribe, Samuel. Mater cara epistulam amat. Pater quoque bonus est.
sentences.english: Write, Samuel. Your dear mother loves a letter. Your father is good too.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Bene! Gratias tibi ago, Martha. Panem et lac emo.
sentences.english: Good! Thank you, Martha. I buy bread and milk.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Vale, Samuel! Pax tibi. Ecce panis, ecce lac. Panem et lac tibi do.
sentences.english: Goodbye, Samuel! Peace to you. Look, bread, look, milk. I give you bread and milk.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Gratias tibi ago! Bene valeo, et fessus non sum.
sentences.english: Thank you! I am well, and I am not tired.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Salvete! Quomodo valetis? Ubi est Lucius?
sentences.english: Hello! How are you? Where is Lucius?
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Bene valemus, Anna. Lucius in schola est.
sentences.english: We are well, Anna. Lucius is at school.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Bene! Panem et lac emo. Gratias tibi ago, Martha. Vale, Samuel!
sentences.english: Good! I buy bread and milk. Thank you, Martha. Goodbye, Samuel!
sentences.speaker: ana
